notes.text: Cancelled typescript draft, manuscript page 19, sections 2.1.1–2.2.3, with the added title Sections unité. The final sentence ends at on note. No date or total page count appears. The archive number is 26 in the opposite orientation, retained only in a comment. H supplies a description only, so this page has no H collation rows; its tentative 92 is an orientation issue in that description.
notes.basis: Three full readings; main archive-number crop; source conventions.

notes.text: The page describes two partially defined composition laws on a G_(P×Q)-torsor E, states equivariance and interchange formulas, and introduces two unit sections followed by a common neutral section. The abandoned scalar formula is preserved through its unfinished phi(. These are reports of source content, not proofs of the full biextension definition.

notes.text: Main reads the second-law sign as psi at the opening, in the following prose, and at all three occurrences in the interchange formula, from the pen shaft through the interior of each typed u-shaped cup. r2 agrees; r1/r3 retain mu/psi initially and use mu at the recurrences under the recurring-sign convention. The separate circled marginal psi/Psi remains uncertain as to case. The mathematical form of the law does not decide these glyphs.

notes.text: The c/s, G/g, and C/c initial overprints retain both possible strike orders. The repeated E and its separately cancelled t are distinguished. In the final display the cancelled lower tail is resolved as /S, but the separately cancelled argument tail remains /S), /P), or /Q). The words et une conséquence and their leading comma remain cancelled and are resolved from the surviving type.

notes.text: A targeted coordinate check of the interchange display passes under the page’s stated partial group-law conventions. With x,y,z,t over (p,q),(p,q′),(p′,q),(p′,q′), both phi(psi(x,y),psi(z,t)) and psi(phi(x,z),phi(y,t)) are defined over (pp′,qq′). This checks domains and indices only; it does not prove existence of a biextension structure.

notes.event_outcome: Passed conditionally: all inner and outer operations have matching required coordinates, and both sides lie over (pp′,qq′). No existence or full-axiom theorem proved.

notes.text: Under the extension conventions stated immediately above, the source’s two named unit sections are paired with the opposite axes. For a concrete test, let S be a point, P=Z/2, Q=Z/3, G trivial, E=P×Q. Then e_(E/P)(p)=(p,0_Q) lies on P×1_Q and has domain P; it cannot be the named section over 1_P×Q, whose domain is Q. The second pairing is reversed in the same way. This refutes the literal pairing under those conventions, without changing the transcription or using an external version.
notes.basis: Actual main-reader domain argument and explicit finite-group counterexample in decisions/scan027_math_work.md; refined statement s027-note09.

notes.text: The refined conditional statement pairs e_(E/P) with P×1_Q and e_(E/Q) with 1_P×Q. Each follows directly by composing the relevant group-extension unit with its projection. Equivalently, one may keep the source’s axes in their order and interchange the names of the two sections. This is a research note only.

notes.text: A limited targeted proof confirms equality of the two units on the common-origin fibre from interchange and the unit axioms. If a is the phi-unit and b the psi-unit there, then a=phi(a,a)=phi(psi(a,b),psi(b,a))=psi(phi(a,b),phi(b,a))=psi(b,b)=b. This does not supply the missing continuation after on note or verify the whole construction.
notes.event_outcome: Passed conditionally on the displayed interchange identity and two unit axioms, restricted to the common-origin fibre; each equality follows from a unit identity or interchange.
